clue.text: Farming editors need to be changed

definitions.text: Farming editors need to be changed

indicators.note: the words are told they must be altered, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A publisher decides its agricultural journalists must be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: farming editors, once altered, become a word meaning altered beyond recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmogrified means transformed, especially in a surprising or grotesque way, which is what happens to the jumbled letters here.

clue.text: Reform of tax is still at hand next year, ending with …

definitions.note: the book, identified by how it ends: the following clues quote its last line

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the following letters are put into a new order

parts.words: tax is still at hand next
parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A tax reform is on the way next year, and the sentence trails off for the next clue to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 1066 and All That is Sellar and Yeatman's 1930 spoof of school history; its last line says America became top nation and history came to a full stop, which 2, 14 down and 12 across spell out.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic history book famously finishes with America as top nation and history halting, so naming its ending identifies the title.

clue.text: … the Queen in some friendly country 14 down

definitions.note: the country that, in the book, became top nation

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other
only some of the word is wanted, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: amicable means friendly
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The monarch visits a friendly nation which is the world's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue carries on from 1 down: the book closes with the line 'America was thus clearly top nation'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1066 and All That, the United States is the country declared top nation at the close of the book.

clue.text: … 1,19's authors dispose of a lecherous oriental divine

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it
taken as written
randy means lustful
E for eastern
atman is the divine self or soul in Hindu thought

explanation.surface: The writers get rid of a lustful holy man from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: W. C. Sellar and R. J. Yeatman wrote 1066 and All That; the leading dots carry on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sellar and Robert Yeatman co-wrote the comic history book given at 1 and 19 down.

clue.text: Love would pass to the expert

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
the old contraction of would, as in Shakespeare's I'ld
to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A lover would hand on their affection to a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle piece is the archaic short form of would, seen in I'ld, rather than the modern 'd.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is a veteran with long experience, someone skilled at a task.

clue.text: Painter to hold up vase

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to bear a weight is to hold it
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to keep a pot aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Raeburn was the Scottish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Raeburn was an eighteenth-century Scottish portrait artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Thematic presentation of air that's close to the top line

definitions.note: adjectival: in the manner of a fugue

parts.note: fug is stuffy, close air
A is the top grade
L is an abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A musical theme set out in a tune near the top of the stave.
explanation.walkthrough: Close here means muggy, not near; air is atmosphere, not a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue develops a subject through successive voices, so fugal describes music built on that kind of thematic treatment.

clue.text: Picked up instruction to strike out and 19 is included

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the whole is read from the bottom
something included is put inside another word

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to delete
and all that means et cetera

explanation.surface: An editor collected a deletion note with an etcetera tucked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 19 is ALL THAT, so 'and 19' reads 'and all that', the familiar Latin abbreviation. It sits just after the first letter of the proofreader's mark before everything is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elected means chosen by vote, and more generally selected, a synonym of picked.

clue.text: Reliable policeman prospered quickly without taking the pledge

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a business that booms grows fast
taking the pledge means swearing off drink, becoming teetotal

explanation.surface: A trustworthy officer got rich fast without giving up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottomed means thoroughly sound and trustworthy, from ships sheathed in copper below the waterline.

clue.text: Goaded to ensure want had priority

parts.note: a want is a need
to have priority is to lead

explanation.surface: Someone was prodded so that their wishes came first.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or irritate them, much as goading does.

clue.text: Painter or composer missing a green opening

indicators.note: the composer is lacking something, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Edward Elgar, English composer
the letter to be removed
eco- is the green prefix that opens words like ecosystem

explanation.surface: Choosing between an artist and a musician who has missed an environmental launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter or composer' looks like a choice of two definitions; only the painter is one.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Toledo, an example of a painter.

clue.text: Island where business comes first?

parts.note: surface reading: a place where commerce takes priority
setter's reading: the short slang form of business appears near the very front of the island's name

explanation.walkthrough: Biz is slang for business, and it sits right at the start of the name after a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, famous for its clubbing industry.

clue.text: Post-historical period after 2 became 14 down

parts.note: surface reading: an era coming after history
setter's reading: period as punctuation, what history came to once America was top nation

explanation.walkthrough: The book's final words: 'America was thus clearly top nation, and History came to a .' Period is the American word for the dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A period is the punctuation mark ending a sentence, and the book says history itself came to one.

clue.text: Trombonist's place for alfresco drinking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jack ..., American jazz trombonist
second meaning: an outdoor cafe serving tea

explanation.surface: A jazz player's favourite spot for an outdoor drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Teagarden led the jazz trombone in the swing era, and a tea garden is an open-air place serving refreshments.

clue.text: Welsh house party gets into the groove when reorientated

indicators.note: one thing getting into another means it is placed inside
turned to face the other way, so the result runs right to left

parts.note: a rut is a groove
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Revellers in a Welsh home find their rhythm after a change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: House means a royal dynasty; the Tudors came from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor dynasty, founded by Henry VII, had Welsh roots, making it a royal line of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Inn with potato being cooked is world leader

indicators.note: food being cooked is transformed, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub's potato dish is the best on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The country at the top of the global order is the leading power on Earth.

clue.text: Having eye trouble because badly housed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: afflicted with a stye on the eyelid
second meaning: kept in a pigsty

explanation.surface: Someone's eyes suffer from their poor living conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an eyelid infection, and to sty is to lodge someone in a pigsty, squalid accommodation.

clue.text: See 3
Holy man takes the blame when his house gets round to torture

parts.note: ST for saint
take the rap means take the blame
pad is slang for a home
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A saint carries the can as his home becomes a torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The strappado hoisted a victim by the wrists tied behind the back and let them drop.
explanation.definitionFit: The strappado was a historical method of inflicting pain by suspension from a rope.

clue.text: Painter doing not so well with model

parts.note: more ill
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: An artist struggling in health alongside his sitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Model suggests the artist's sitter, but it is the Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was an English painter of the Camden Town Group, an example of a painter.

clue.text: Broadland village made her change

indicators.note: the letters are told to alter, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman was forced to transform in the Norfolk countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadland is the Norfolk Broads, a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedham is a riverside village on the Yare in the Norfolk Broads area.

clue.text: See 1
10p newspaper piece on the meson

parts.note: X is the Roman ten, and p stands for penny
an article is a piece in a paper

explanation.surface: A cheap daily runs a feature about particle physics.
explanation.definitionFit: X-particle was an early name for the meson, the subatomic particle predicted by Yukawa.

clue.text: It takes 2 to make sunburn disappear

parts.note: a tan is skin darkened by sun
to go is to vanish

explanation.surface: You need a partner to get rid of sun damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition finishes the saying 'it takes two to tango'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a dance for a couple needs both partners, so this dance completes the familiar phrase.

clue.text: Give as portion of vote without leader

indicators.note: lacking its leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

explanation.surface: Hand out a share of a leaderless election.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute something in shares, assigning each recipient a part.

clue.text: He should get the job of a setter with another one outside

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
a different version of the word, so its letters are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written
belonging to the setter, who speaks as me

explanation.surface: A candidate is chosen for a post, with a crossword compiler in the frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria often uses 'another one' for a rearranged ONE; its first two letters and last letter go either side of the setter's possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for a position, the person expected to be appointed.

clue.text: He finds Haig unhappily married in Broadland potter's village

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an unhappy state suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
M for married

explanation.surface: A man discovers Haig in a bad marriage in a Norfolk village.
explanation.walkthrough: A potter here is someone pottering about by boat on the Broads, the Norfolk waterways; Heigham Sound is a lake there.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigham is a place on the Norfolk Broads, around Heigham Sound near Potter Heigham, popular with boating holidaymakers.

clue.text: Model dictator in … in his shirt sleeves is still pure

indicators.note: the first pieces are set inside the following phrase

parts.note: without a jacket
the ellipsis apparently stands for a letter left out of the clue
the Model T Ford
Idi Amin, Ugandan dictator

explanation.surface: A tyrant in casual dress remains untainted.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the wordplay is a letter short: the inserted part needs an N before the car and the dictator, which the dots appear to stand for.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontaminated means free from any polluting substance, which is what pure means.
